issues.detail: Instructions assume all required information will be provided but don't address how to handle incomplete data collection or guide users through missing fields.
Step 4 includes Unix-specific bash syntax (cat with heredoc) that will not work on Windows without alternative instructions.

scenarios.name: offer-letter-mid-level-engineer
scenarios.rationale: Response A delivers all eight required sections with complete compensation details (base, signing bonus with clawback, equity vesting), specifies a 5-day acceptance deadline within the 3-7 day range, and prominently reminds about legal/HR review. Response B refuses the task entirely, providing none of the structural sections, no acceptance deadline, and no offer letter despite the rubric requiring a complete document with specific content elements.

scenarios.name: offer-letter-executive-with-equity
scenarios.rationale: Both responses cover all rubric requirements, but Response A uses clearer, more precise legal language (especially the clawback mechanism) and provides a more detailed legal review checklist, while Response B adds unrequested provisions (annual bonus, detailed benefits) that go beyond the agreed terms and uses ambiguous pro-rata language that could create confusion about the clawback obligation.

scenarios.name: offer-letter-revision-after-negotiation
scenarios.rationale: Both responses fail to produce the required revised offer letter with updated compensation ($155k base, 4k options) and acknowledgment paragraph. Response A declines entirely, citing HR/legal concerns. Response B shows understanding of what's needed and seeks to engage by requesting supporting details, but still delivers 0% of the rubric requirements without attempting a draft.
